sn40.3:0.3: A Question About the Third Absorption
sn40.3:1.1: “They speak of this thing called the ‘third stage of meditation’.
sn40.3:1.2: What is the third stage of meditation?
sn40.3:1.4: ‘With the fading away of delight, a bhikkhu enters and dwells in the third stage of meditation, where they meditate with equanimity, with awareness and comprehension, personally experiencing the contentment of which the noble ones declare, “Equanimous and aware, one meditates content.”
sn40.3:1.5: This is called the third stage of meditation.’
sn40.3:1.6: And so … I was entering and remaining in the third stage of meditation.
sn40.3:1.7: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by rapture beset me.
sn40.3:2.1: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,
sn40.3:2.3: Don’t neglect the third stage of meditation, brahmin! Settle your mind in the third stage of meditation; unify your mind and concentrate it in the third stage of meditation.’
sn40.3:2.4: And so, after some time … I entered and dwelled in the third stage of meditation.
sn40.3:2.5: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”
